user.title: IR Hub — transmitter type & setup mode
user.description:
Bundled library: {devices} key-based remotes + a full AC state-code library.

**Transmitter type**: a self-built ESPHome infrared emitter (recommended), an off-the-shelf Broadlink, an MQTT gateway running Tasmota IRMQTTServer, or any ESPHome action that accepts raw timings (SmartAC-compatible).

**Setup mode**: Manual = browse category → brand → model; Pair with remote = point the ORIGINAL remote at an IR receiver, press a key, and the code is looked up automatically (works for key-based devices AND air conditioners; much faster when the model is unknown).

tx.title: IR Hub — Transmitter target & device type

brand.title: IR Hub — brand
brand.description: Category: {category} — {count} brands have codes here (busiest first).

device.title: IR Hub — model
device.description:
{brand} — {count} models. The protocol hint is informational only: the real carrier is often different, so test 38 kHz first.

The next step transmits a test frame — keep the device in line of sight.

test.title: IR Hub — Test frame sent
test.description:
**A test frame (key: {key}) was just sent to {brand} ({index}/{total}: {model}).**

Watch the device: if it reacted (power on / LED blink / action), pick "It worked" to finish; otherwise "Try next model automatically" (great for set-top boxes with many models) or go back and pick manually. Choose "Skip" if you are not near the device.

learn_setup.title: IR Hub — Pair with remote: receiver & category
learn_setup.description:
Channel: **{tx_type}**
Target: {tx_target_hint}

Pick the **IR receiver** (library date: {generated}) and the **device category**.

⚠️ Point the original remote at the receiver, 5–30 cm away. The category matters: matching only searches WITHIN it, so a wrong category finds nothing. Air conditioners can be paired too: pick "Air conditioner · thermostat" and press the POWER key on the AC remote.

learn_press.title: IR Hub — Key {seq}: press the remote
learn_press.description:
Receiver: **{receiver}**
State: `{receiver_state}`{subscribe_error}

Point the original remote AT the receiver above, press **{key_hint}**, then Submit.

> "{captured} frames captured" is a SNAPSHOT taken when this page opened — you press the remote afterwards, so it usually shows 0 and does NOT mean nothing was received. The frames actually used for matching are listed on the next screen.

> The state is the probe: after pressing the remote it should turn into a timestamp. Unchanged = the frame never reached HA (the dropdown points at another device, or that device is offline). Changed but still "no signal" = the problem is in this integration; please report that line.

learn_press2.title: IR Hub — Key {seq} (optional): narrow the model
learn_press2.description:
Receiver: **{receiver}**
State: `{receiver_state}`{subscribe_error}

Press **{key_hint}** once more and submit — intersecting both keys throws away most of the same-code / near-code models (air conditioners especially: same protocol family cannot be told apart from the power key alone).

Pick "skip" to match on the power key only (more candidates). Again, "{captured} frames captured" is a snapshot from when this page opened.

learn_pick.title: IR Hub — Confirm the matched model

learn_test.title: IR Hub — Confirm with a test frame
learn_test.description:
**A test frame (key: {key}) was just sent to {model}.**

Pick "It worked" to finish; otherwise "Back to candidates" to try the next-best candidate.

ac_brand.title: IR Hub — Pick an AC brand
ac_brand.description:
Air conditioners use the irext state-code library ({count} brands / {devices} models).

You will get a **real thermostat panel** (native mode/temperature/fan controls) — no SmartIR/SmartAC needed.

ac_device.title: IR Hub — Pick an AC model
ac_device.description:
{brand} — {count} models (numbers from the irext library).

If some commands don't work, try a different carrier frequency in the integration options.

ac_test_on.title: IR Hub — AC power-ON test frame sent
ac_test_on.description:
**An ON frame (26°C / auto fan) was just sent ({brand} · candidate {index}/{total}: model {model}).**

If the AC beeped or started blowing, pick "It worked" — an OFF frame follows for a second confirmation; otherwise "Try next model automatically" or go back and pick manually. Choose "Skip" if you are not near the unit.

ac_test.title: IR Hub — AC power-OFF test frame sent
ac_test.description:
**An OFF frame was just sent ({brand} · candidate {index}/{total}: model {model}).**

If the AC beeped or powered down, pick "It worked" to finish; otherwise "Try next model automatically" or go back and pick manually. Choose "Skip" if you are not near the unit.

abort.no_emitters: No infrared emitter found. Add an ESPHome device with an `infrared:` entity (platform `ir_rf_proxy`) first, then reload this integration.
abort.empty_library: The bundled code library is empty or unreadable.
abort.no_brands: This category has no brands in the code library.
abort.no_devices: This brand has no models in the code library.
abort.device_gone: That model is no longer in the code library.
abort.ac_decode_failed: This model's code data failed to decode (corrupt irext data). Try another model.
abort.test_exhausted: Every model in this brand was tried with no reaction — check aim/line of sight, try another carrier (56k) in the options, or pick a different brand.
abort.no_receivers: No infrared receiver found. Add a receiver entity on an ESPHome device (an `infrared:` entry using `ir_rf_proxy`, or `remote_receiver` plus an infrared platform) first, then reload this integration.
abort.receiver_api_missing: This Home Assistant version's infrared integration has no RECEIVER API yet (receiving was added after the 2026.4 emitter support). Upgrade Home Assistant to a version with the IR receiver entity, or use "Manual" setup.
abort.learn_no_match: No model matched in the selected category. Check: (1) is the category correct (matching only searches within it); (2) is the remote aimed at the receiver (5–30 cm); (3) does the library even contain this remote (try "Manual" and browse by brand).

error.send_failed: Sending the test frame failed (emitter offline or refused). Retry later, skip the test, or go back.
error.no_test_key: This model has no usable test code in the library. You can skip the test and finish anyway.
error.target_missing: The transmitter target does not exist or is unavailable (entity offline / ESPHome action not registered / Broadlink entity missing). Check and retry.
error.mqtt_missing: The MQTT integration is not loaded — configure an MQTT broker in HA first, then use the MQTT channel.
error.no_signal:
No infrared signal captured. Point the remote AT the receiver (5-30 cm), press again, then submit again. Check the batteries too.

Still nothing? Look at the "state" line above: after pressing the remote it should turn into a timestamp. Unchanged = the frame never reached HA (wrong receiver picked — another device — or that device is offline). Changed but still "no signal" here = the problem is in this integration; please report that line.
error.subscribe_failed: **Could not subscribe to the receiver.** Go back one step and pick another receiver (the dropdown shows which device each one belongs to); see the note above for the exact reason.
error.receiver_unavailable: The selected receiver entity does not exist, or that device is offline (see the state line above). Go back one step and make sure the dropdown points at the device you are aiming at.

init.title: IR Hub settings
init.description:
Settings for {title}.

Carrier: most devices use 38000 Hz. Do NOT trust the protocol name in the library — if the device ignores the codes, try 56000 (or 40000) here.
Transmit count: how many times the frame is sent per press (1 = once). RAISE this if the device only responds every other press.
Broadlink delay: only used by the Broadlink channel (seconds between sends).
MQTT payload format: MQTT channel only. smartac = bare timing array (tcl-ir style bridges, default); tasmota = Tasmota IRMQTTServer RAW JSON.
